errors.problem: This is the normalized total, the cost divided by V. The actual total is O(V pK^{tau-1}). The paper says "so the normalized total is O(p/K)K^tau=O(pK^{tau-1})".

errors.quote: Each move peels one excess bit, exchanges the equal-width parts and restores it, costing $O(V(1+\ell^\tau))$
errors.problem: The paper peels a single excess bit only "when widths differ by one". When the two axis widths are equal there is no excess bit, and the parts are exchanged directly.

errors.quote: because $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ beats every power of $p$
errors.problem: Taken literally this is false, because K is itself a small power of p. What beats every fixed power of p is 2^K, so 2^{-K}p^{O(1)}=o(1). The paper says only "K=Theta(p^{epsilon c}) with epsilon c>0" in front of the bound O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V).

errors.quote: Let $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ be the volume, the number of stored bits of $T$ coefficients of $p$ bits
errors.problem: The paper's fixed-width formats use Theta(p) bits per coefficient, so a full padded array has Theta(V) stored bits. V=Tp is the normalizing volume, not exactly the stored bit count.
